title: What does it mean to have relationship ambivalence?
titleZh: 对一段关系既爱又厌，意味着什么？

sentence_pairs.en: When a relationship provokes both strong positive and negative feelings in you, it can take a toll – here’s what’s going on
sentence_pairs.cn: 当一段关系同时激起你强烈的好感与恶感，它是会消耗人的——这里讲讲这到底是怎么回事

sentence_pairs.en: We tend to talk about our relationships as either satisfying or unsatisfying, healthy or toxic.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我们谈论自己的关系时，总爱二选一：满意或不满意，健康或有毒。

sentence_pairs.en: This either/or perspective shapes a lot of relationship advice, and filters through to the ways many of us chat about our relationship dilemmas with friends.
sentence_pairs.cn: 这种非此即彼的视角塑造了大量关于关系的建议，也渗透进我们许多人向朋友倾诉关系难题的方式里。

sentence_pairs.en: But the reality is that many of our most consequential relationships in life are both positive and negative at the same time (or neither positive nor negative – which I’ll come back to later).
sentence_pairs.cn: 但现实是，我们生命中许多最重要的关系，是同时既正面又负面的（或者既不正面也不负面——这一点我后面还会谈到）。

sentence_pairs.en: You can love your partner tremendously and hate their lack of responsibility.
sentence_pairs.cn: 你可以深爱你的伴侣，又痛恨他缺乏责任感。

sentence_pairs.en: You can feel deeply grateful to your in-laws for all the support they offer while at the same time feeling extremely annoyed by their intrusiveness.
sentence_pairs.cn: 你可以对岳家、婆家提供的种种支持深怀感激，同时又为他们的处处干涉恼火不已。

sentence_pairs.en: You can admire your boss’s effectiveness and be irritated by their micromanaging.
sentence_pairs.cn: 你可以佩服上司的干练，又被他的事事插手弄得烦躁。

sentence_pairs.en: My colleagues and I recently put forward a new four-quadrant framework for how people evaluate their relationships.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我和同事们最近提出了一个评估人际关系的新四象限框架。

sentence_pairs.en: The experiences I just described would fall into the ambivalent quadrant, which is characterised by having both strong positive and negative feelings toward another person at the same time.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我刚描述的这些体验就落在"矛盾心理"（ambivalent）那一象限，它的特征是对同一个人同时怀有强烈的正面和负面感受。

sentence_pairs.en: The other quadrants are feeling mostly positive, mostly negative or indifferent.
sentence_pairs.cn: 另外三个象限分别是：以正面为主、以负面为主，以及无感。

sentence_pairs.en: We believe that ambivalence in relationships has been largely overlooked up until now, even though it’s such a common and consequential experience.
sentence_pairs.cn: 我们认为，关系中的矛盾心理尽管如此常见、影响如此之大，却在此前基本被忽视了。

sentence_pairs.en: It’s important to say that being in an ambivalent relationship is not the same as finding it mildly satisfying – the distinctive nature of these relationships is that you experience strong positive feelings and strong negative feelings.
sentence_pairs.cn: 需要说明的是，身处一段矛盾的关系，并不等于对它还算满意——这类关系的独特之处在于，你会同时体验到强烈的正面感受和强烈的负面感受。

sentence_pairs.en: It’s also important to distinguish ambivalence from indifference, which occurs when neither positive nor negative feelings are strong and the relationship instead feels emotionally neutral.
sentence_pairs.cn: 同样重要的是要把矛盾心理与冷漠（indifference）区分开：冷漠是正面与负面感受都不强烈，这段关系在情感上近乎中性。

sentence_pairs.en: In other words, ambivalence is ‘I care a lot, but I’m torn,’ while indifference is closer to ‘I’m not especially drawn in, upset, or emotionally invested.’
sentence_pairs.cn: 换句话说，矛盾是"我很在乎，但我被撕扯着"，而冷漠更接近"我既不特别投入，也不特别沮丧，没有任何情感押注"。

sentence_pairs.en: How does ambivalence arise in relationships?
sentence_pairs.cn: 矛盾心理是如何在关系中产生的？

sentence_pairs.en: Certainly, some relationships are a mixed package from their very beginning: offering great warmth and connection alongside quirks, costs or complications that never quite disappear.
sentence_pairs.cn: 当然，有些关系从一开始就是一个混合包裹：它给出巨大的温暖与联结，同时也附带那些从未彻底消失的怪癖、代价或麻烦。

sentence_pairs.en: Since their start, they stir both gratitude and frustration, attraction and hesitation.
sentence_pairs.cn: 从一开始，它们就同时搅动着感激与沮丧、吸引与犹豫。

sentence_pairs.en: But ambivalence can also grow over time.
sentence_pairs.cn: 但矛盾心理也会随着时间生长。

sentence_pairs.en: Relationships evolve and studies show that even relationships that start out mostly positive (such as romantic relationships) often accumulate negative feelings as life unfolds and significant challenges emerge.
sentence_pairs.cn: 关系会演变，而研究表明，即使一开始以正面为主的关系（比如恋爱关系），也会随着生活的展开和重大挑战的出现，累积起负面感受。

sentence_pairs.en: Partners change, circumstances shift, responsibilities grow heavier.
sentence_pairs.cn: 伴侣会变，境遇会变，责任会越来越重。

sentence_pairs.en: What once felt effortless now involves compromises, mismatched needs or recurring patterns we didn’t see in the early glow.
sentence_pairs.cn: 曾经毫不费力的事，如今充满了妥协、错位的需求，或是在早期光环里看不见的、反复出现的模式。

sentence_pairs.en: When these negative feelings first emerge, the positive ones do not suddenly dissipate, thus creating ambivalence.
sentence_pairs.cn: 当这些负面感受初次浮现时，正面感受并不会骤然消散——矛盾心理由此产生。

sentence_pairs.en: Think about a relationship in your own life that leaves you feeling torn.
sentence_pairs.cn: 想一想你自己生活中那段让你倍感撕扯的关系。

sentence_pairs.en: Maybe you care deeply about this person and value the bond, yet also feel hurt, frustrated or disappointed by them.
sentence_pairs.cn: 也许你深切在乎这个人、珍视这份联结，却也常被他伤害、惹恼或失望。

sentence_pairs.en: If that feels unsettling, our findings suggest there is a reason: people are often distressed by the mixed feelings of relationship ambivalence.
sentence_pairs.cn: 如果这让你感到不安，我们的研究结果表明这是有原因的：关系矛盾心理带来的复杂感受，常常令人痛苦。

sentence_pairs.en: We do not want to feel pulled in opposite directions about someone who matters to us.
sentence_pairs.cn: 对一个对我们重要的人，我们不愿感到自己被拉向两个相反的方向。

sentence_pairs.en: In fact, our studies (and research by others) have shown that ambivalence in romantic relationships undermines both relationship quality and personal wellbeing.
sentence_pairs.cn: 事实上，我们的研究（以及其他人的研究）都显示，亲密关系中的矛盾心理会同时损害关系质量和个人幸福感。

sentence_pairs.en: And the strain is not only psychological: experiencing ambivalence has been linked to higher blood pressure, greater inflammation and other early markers of cardiovascular risk.
sentence_pairs.cn: 而且这种消耗不只是心理上的：处于矛盾心理状态，已被发现与更高的血压、更严重的炎症以及其他心血管风险的早期指标相关。

sentence_pairs.en: Despite this tension, we’ve found that ambivalence doesn’t tend to mean that people check out of a relationship – if anything, it often means the opposite.
sentence_pairs.cn: 尽管有这些撕扯，我们发现矛盾心理并不意味着人们会从关系中抽身离开——如果说有什么倾向，它往往意味着相反的结果。

sentence_pairs.en: When someone feels both pulled in and pushed away, they tend to stay mentally busy trying to ‘solve’ the ambivalence: they want to either like or dislike someone; they want to figure out whether the relationship is worth investment or whether it is best to pull away.
sentence_pairs.cn: 当一个人既被吸引又被推拒时，他的头脑往往忙着去"解决"这种矛盾：他想么喜欢这个人，要么讨厌这个人；他想弄清楚这段关系值不值得投入，还是趁早抽身为好。

sentence_pairs.en: In fact, in our studies we found that the more ambivalence someone experiences in a romantic relationship, the more they think and ruminate about it.
sentence_pairs.cn: 事实上，在我们的研究中我们发现：一个人在亲密关系中体验到的矛盾心理越多，他对这段关系的思考和反刍就越多。

sentence_pairs.en: These ruminative thoughts tend to swing in two directions.
sentence_pairs.cn: 这些反刍式的念头往往在两个方向上摇摆。

sentence_pairs.en: At times they are constructive and people think about ways to improve things, fix patterns, reconnect.
sentence_pairs.cn: 有时它们是建设性的：人们会想怎么改善、怎么修正模式、怎么重新联结。

sentence_pairs.en: Other times, their thoughts are pretty destructive, focusing on all the difficulties, problems and flaws of the relationships.
sentence_pairs.cn: 另一些时候，这些念头相当具有破坏性，聚焦于这段关系的所有困难、问题和缺陷。

sentence_pairs.en: That same push‑pull shows up in behaviour.
sentence_pairs.cn: 同样的推拉也体现在行为上。

sentence_pairs.en: Some days people act warmly and constructively, trying to connect with the other person.
sentence_pairs.cn: 有些日子，人们表现得温暖而有建设性，努力与对方建立联结。

sentence_pairs.en: On other days, people are destructive, by withdrawing or blaming and criticising others.
sentence_pairs.cn: 另一些日子，人们则具有破坏性——退缩，或者指责、批评对方。

sentence_pairs.en: And in our studies that have tracked people over time, we see that ambivalence reliably produces these swings, making people fluctuate substantially between these two different types of thoughts and behaviours on a daily basis.
sentence_pairs.cn: 在那些对人们进行长期追踪的研究中，我们看到矛盾心理会稳定地制造这种摇摆，让人每天在这两类截然不同的想法和行为之间大幅波动。

sentence_pairs.en: So feeling ambivalent does not seem like a walk in the woods.
sentence_pairs.cn: 所以，心怀矛盾看来并不是一次轻松的林间漫步。

sentence_pairs.en: It is stressful and consequential for how people behave in their relationship.
sentence_pairs.cn: 它是有压力的，也实实在在地影响着人们在关系中的行为。

sentence_pairs.en: And what about the person on the receiving end?
sentence_pairs.cn: 那么，处在接受端的那个人的感受呢？

sentence_pairs.en: What happens when your partner has both strong positive and strong negative feelings toward you: one day they want to connect, the next they pull back or critique, and the cycle repeats?
sentence_pairs.cn: 当你的伴侣对你同时怀有强烈的好感与恶感——今天想靠近，明天就疏远或挑剔，循环往复——会发生什么？

sentence_pairs.en: Being on the receiving end of those mixed signals can feel destabilising.
sentence_pairs.cn: 不断接收这些混杂的信号，会让人觉得天旋地转。

sentence_pairs.en: And those shifts – from connection to distance, from support to irritation – aren’t just confusing; they can take a toll on the sense of safety and stability in the relationship.
sentence_pairs.cn: 而这些摇摆——从联结到疏远，从支持到烦躁——不只是令人困惑；它们会侵蚀这段关系里的安全感与稳定感。

sentence_pairs.en: In fact, in our studies , we find that recipients of ambivalence often experience their partner as unpredictable and hard to read.
sentence_pairs.cn: 事实上，在我们的研究中，处于矛盾心理接受端的人，常常觉得自己的伴侣难以预测、难以读懂。

sentence_pairs.en: That uncertainty doesn’t just chip away at relationship quality, it also affects the wellbeing of the recipient of the ambivalence.
sentence_pairs.cn: 这种不确定性不只是蚕食关系质量，它也影响被矛盾波及者的身心健康。

sentence_pairs.en: Recipients report feeling more stressed, in a more negative mood, and less satisfied with their lives overall.
sentence_pairs.cn: 接受端的人报告说，自己压力更大、情绪更消极，对生活的整体满意度也更低。

sentence_pairs.en: It’s clear that ambivalence isn’t a solo experience, it tends to spill over, influencing (and potentially damaging) the person on the other side of the relationship, too.
sentence_pairs.cn: 显然，矛盾心理不是一个人的独角戏——它往往会外溢，波及（甚至伤害）关系另一端的那个人的感受。

sentence_pairs.en: If you recognise these descriptions of relationship ambivalence including the challenges involved, you might be wondering if there’s anything you can do about it.
sentence_pairs.cn: 如果你在上述对关系矛盾心理的描述（包括其中的种种困境）里认出了自己，你也许想知道：对此能做点什么吗？

sentence_pairs.en: There’s no quick fix, but there is some good news.
sentence_pairs.cn: 没有速效药，但有一些好消息。

sentence_pairs.en: First, ambivalence means that the relationship matters to you.
sentence_pairs.cn: 首先，矛盾心理意味着这段关系对你很重要。

sentence_pairs.en: Mixed feelings – strong positives and strong negatives – show up only when someone is important to us.
sentence_pairs.cn: 混合的感受——强烈的正面与强烈的负面——只会在一个人对我们很重要的时候出现。

sentence_pairs.en: If the relationship didn’t matter to you, you wouldn’t feel torn; you would feel indifferent.
sentence_pairs.cn: 如果这段关系对你无关紧要，你不会感到撕扯；你会无感。

sentence_pairs.en: Indifference is the state where even the negative feelings have faded – you’re no longer frustrated or hurt, you’ve simply stopped noticing.
sentence_pairs.cn: 冷漠是连负面感受都已褪去的状态——你不再沮丧，不再受伤，你只是不再注意了。

sentence_pairs.en: So ambivalence, uncomfortable as it is, signals that this is still a meaningful relationship.
sentence_pairs.cn: 所以，矛盾心理虽然令人不适，却表明这仍是一段有意义的关系。

sentence_pairs.en: Second, ambivalence makes you reflect on the relationship.
sentence_pairs.cn: 其次，矛盾心理促使你反思这段关系。

sentence_pairs.en: You are involved, you want to understand what is going on, and decide what should happen next.
sentence_pairs.cn: 你是投入其中的，你想弄明白发生了什么，并决定接下来该怎么办。

sentence_pairs.en: Ambivalence is an important signal that shows you that a rewarding and valuable relationship poses significant costs too, nudging you to ask whether to repair, recalibrate or step back.
sentence_pairs.cn: 矛盾心理是一个重要的信号：它告诉你，一段有回报、有价值的关系同时也意味着不小的代价，它推着你去追问——是修复，是重新调整，还是退后一步。

sentence_pairs.en: All this means that if you are now recognising for the first time that a significant relationship in your life is ambivalent for you, this awareness is already an important first step.
sentence_pairs.cn: 这一切意味着，如果你此刻第一次意识到：自己生命中某段重要的关系让你心怀矛盾，那么这份觉察本身已经是重要的第一步。

sentence_pairs.en: Becoming aware of your mixed feelings creates an opportunity to reflect on the relationship.
sentence_pairs.cn: 觉察到自己的复杂感受，为反思这段关系创造了机会。

sentence_pairs.en: This is a good moment to intervene and influence what happens next.
sentence_pairs.cn: 此时正是介入并影响后续走向的好时机。

sentence_pairs.en: After all, if you are having these mixed feelings, it means two helpful conditions are present:
sentence_pairs.cn: 毕竟，你之所以有这些复杂感受，说明两个有利条件已经具备：

sentence_pairs.en: There’s still some positivity to build on.
sentence_pairs.cn: 其一，还有一些积极面可供依托。

sentence_pairs.en: The relationship has rewards; the task is to reduce the negativity, not to build positivity from scratch; and
sentence_pairs.cn: 这段关系仍有回报；要做的功课是减少消极，而不是从零开始建立积极；并且

sentence_pairs.en: You are still engaged.
sentence_pairs.cn: 其二，你仍然是投入的。

sentence_pairs.en: You care, you’re motivated, and you’re open to making things better – whether through conversation, reflection, counselling or other forms of support (in other words, you are not in the indifferent quadrant of our framework, which would be worse news for the relationship!)
sentence_pairs.cn: 你在乎，你有动力，你也愿意把事情变好——无论是通过交谈、反思、心理咨询还是其他形式的支持（换句话说，你还不在我们框架里的冷漠象限——那对这段关系来说是更坏的消息！）

sentence_pairs.en: If negativity comes to overwhelm the positives – or if you find yourself starting to drift into indifference – then your window for change will have narrowed.
sentence_pairs.cn: 如果负面感受最终压过了正面感受——或者你发现自己开始滑向冷漠——那么你做出改变的窗口就会变窄。

sentence_pairs.en: Ambivalence, in contrast, sits in a workable in‑between zone, where effort still has room to make a difference.
sentence_pairs.cn: 相比之下，矛盾心理恰好坐落在一个仍可着力的中间地带，努力还有空间改变现状。

sentence_pairs.en: It can be a moment to approach the other person, communicate your needs, and see whether you can find ways together that allow the relationship to improve.
sentence_pairs.cn: 它可以成为一个契机：走近对方，说出你的需要，看看你们能否一起找到让关系变好的办法。

sentence_pairs.en: After all, ambivalence is the emotional equivalent of a blinking yellow light: not a stop, not a go, but an invitation to pay attention.
sentence_pairs.cn: 毕竟，矛盾心理在情绪上正是一盏闪烁的黄灯：不是停，不是行，而是一个提醒你留心的邀请。

sentence_pairs.en: And with the right attention, many relationships can still find their better path.
sentence_pairs.cn: 只要给以恰当的关注，许多关系依然能找到更好的那条路。

sentences.cn: 曾经毫不费力的事，如今充满了妥协、错位的需求，或是在早期光环里看不见的、反复出现的模式。

sentences.en: When these negative feelings first emerge, the positive ones do not suddenly dissipate, thus creating ambivalence.
sentences.cn: 当这些负面感受初次浮现时，正面感受并不会骤然消散——矛盾心理由此产生。

sentences.en: Think about a relationship in your own life that leaves you feeling torn.
sentences.cn: 想一想你自己生活中那段让你倍感撕扯的关系。

sentences.en: Maybe you care deeply about this person and value the bond, yet also feel hurt, frustrated or disappointed by them.
sentences.cn: 也许你深切在乎这个人、珍视这份联结，却也常被他伤害、惹恼或失望。

sentences.en: If that feels unsettling, our findings suggest there is a reason: people are often distressed by the mixed feelings of relationship ambivalence.
sentences.cn: 如果这让你感到不安，我们的研究结果表明这是有原因的：关系矛盾心理带来的复杂感受，常常令人痛苦。

sentences.en: We do not want to feel pulled in opposite directions about someone who matters to us.
sentences.cn: 对一个对我们重要的人，我们不愿感到自己被拉向两个相反的方向。

sentences.en: In fact, our studies (and research by others) have shown that ambivalence in romantic relationships undermines both relationship quality and personal wellbeing.
sentences.cn: 事实上，我们的研究（以及其他人的研究）都显示，亲密关系中的矛盾心理会同时损害关系质量和个人幸福感。

sentences.en: And the strain is not only psychological: experiencing ambivalence has been linked to higher blood pressure, greater inflammation and other early markers of cardiovascular risk.
sentences.cn: 而且这种消耗不只是心理上的：处于矛盾心理状态，已被发现与更高的血压、更严重的炎症以及其他心血管风险的早期指标相关。

sentences.en: Despite this tension, we’ve found that ambivalence doesn’t tend to mean that people check out of a relationship – if anything, it often means the opposite.
sentences.cn: 尽管有这些撕扯，我们发现矛盾心理并不意味着人们会从关系中抽身离开——如果说有什么倾向，它往往意味着相反的结果。

sentences.en: When someone feels both pulled in and pushed away, they tend to stay mentally busy trying to ‘solve’ the ambivalence: they want to either like or dislike someone; they want to figure out whether the relationship is worth investment or whether it is best to pull away.
sentences.cn: 当一个人既被吸引又被推拒时，他的头脑往往忙着去"解决"这种矛盾：他想么喜欢这个人，要么讨厌这个人；他想弄清楚这段关系值不值得投入，还是趁早抽身为好。

sentences.en: In fact, in our studies we found that the more ambivalence someone experiences in a romantic relationship, the more they think and ruminate about it.
sentences.cn: 事实上，在我们的研究中我们发现：一个人在亲密关系中体验到的矛盾心理越多，他对这段关系的思考和反刍就越多。

sentences.en: These ruminative thoughts tend to swing in two directions.
sentences.cn: 这些反刍式的念头往往在两个方向上摇摆。

sentences.en: At times they are constructive and people think about ways to improve things, fix patterns, reconnect.
sentences.cn: 有时它们是建设性的：人们会想怎么改善、怎么修正模式、怎么重新联结。

sentences.en: Other times, their thoughts are pretty destructive, focusing on all the difficulties, problems and flaws of the relationships.
sentences.cn: 另一些时候，这些念头相当具有破坏性，聚焦于这段关系的所有困难、问题和缺陷。

sentences.en: That same push‑pull shows up in behaviour.
sentences.cn: 同样的推拉也体现在行为上。

sentences.en: Some days people act warmly and constructively, trying to connect with the other person.
sentences.cn: 有些日子，人们表现得温暖而有建设性，努力与对方建立联结。

sentences.en: On other days, people are destructive, by withdrawing or blaming and criticising others.
sentences.cn: 另一些日子，人们则具有破坏性——退缩，或者指责、批评对方。

sentences.en: And in our studies that have tracked people over time, we see that ambivalence reliably produces these swings, making people fluctuate substantially between these two different types of thoughts and behaviours on a daily basis.
sentences.cn: 在那些对人们进行长期追踪的研究中，我们看到矛盾心理会稳定地制造这种摇摆，让人每天在这两类截然不同的想法和行为之间大幅波动。

sentences.en: So feeling ambivalent does not seem like a walk in the woods.
sentences.cn: 所以，心怀矛盾看来并不是一次轻松的林间漫步。

sentences.en: It is stressful and consequential for how people behave in their relationship.
sentences.cn: 它是有压力的，也实实在在地影响着人们在关系中的行为。

sentences.en: And what about the person on the receiving end?
sentences.cn: 那么，处在接受端的那个人的感受呢？

sentences.en: What happens when your partner has both strong positive and strong negative feelings toward you: one day they want to connect, the next they pull back or critique, and the cycle repeats?
sentences.cn: 当你的伴侣对你同时怀有强烈的好感与恶感——今天想靠近，明天就疏远或挑剔，循环往复——会发生什么？

sentences.en: Being on the receiving end of those mixed signals can feel destabilising.
sentences.cn: 不断接收这些混杂的信号，会让人觉得天旋地转。

sentences.en: And those shifts – from connection to distance, from support to irritation – aren’t just confusing; they can take a toll on the sense of safety and stability in the relationship.
sentences.cn: 而这些摇摆——从联结到疏远，从支持到烦躁——不只是令人困惑；它们会侵蚀这段关系里的安全感与稳定感。

sentences.en: In fact, in our studies , we find that recipients of ambivalence often experience their partner as unpredictable and hard to read.
sentences.cn: 事实上，在我们的研究中，处于矛盾心理接受端的人，常常觉得自己的伴侣难以预测、难以读懂。

sentences.en: That uncertainty doesn’t just chip away at relationship quality, it also affects the wellbeing of the recipient of the ambivalence.
sentences.cn: 这种不确定性不只是蚕食关系质量，它也影响被矛盾波及者的身心健康。

sentences.en: Recipients report feeling more stressed, in a more negative mood, and less satisfied with their lives overall.
sentences.cn: 接受端的人报告说，自己压力更大、情绪更消极，对生活的整体满意度也更低。

sentences.en: It’s clear that ambivalence isn’t a solo experience, it tends to spill over, influencing (and potentially damaging) the person on the other side of the relationship, too.
sentences.cn: 显然，矛盾心理不是一个人的独角戏——它往往会外溢，波及（甚至伤害）关系另一端的那个人的感受。

sentences.en: If you recognise these descriptions of relationship ambivalence including the challenges involved, you might be wondering if there’s anything you can do about it.
sentences.cn: 如果你在上述对关系矛盾心理的描述（包括其中的种种困境）里认出了自己，你也许想知道：对此能做点什么吗？

sentences.en: There’s no quick fix, but there is some good news.
sentences.cn: 没有速效药，但有一些好消息。

sentences.en: First, ambivalence means that the relationship matters to you.
sentences.cn: 首先，矛盾心理意味着这段关系对你很重要。

sentences.en: Mixed feelings – strong positives and strong negatives – show up only when someone is important to us.
sentences.cn: 混合的感受——强烈的正面与强烈的负面——只会在一个人对我们很重要的时候出现。

sentences.en: If the relationship didn’t matter to you, you wouldn’t feel torn; you would feel indifferent.
sentences.cn: 如果这段关系对你无关紧要，你不会感到撕扯；你会无感。

sentences.en: Indifference is the state where even the negative feelings have faded – you’re no longer frustrated or hurt, you’ve simply stopped noticing.
sentences.cn: 冷漠是连负面感受都已褪去的状态——你不再沮丧，不再受伤，你只是不再注意了。

sentences.en: So ambivalence, uncomfortable as it is, signals that this is still a meaningful relationship.
sentences.cn: 所以，矛盾心理虽然令人不适，却表明这仍是一段有意义的关系。

sentences.en: Second, ambivalence makes you reflect on the relationship.
sentences.cn: 其次，矛盾心理促使你反思这段关系。

sentences.en: You are involved, you want to understand what is going on, and decide what should happen next.
sentences.cn: 你是投入其中的，你想弄明白发生了什么，并决定接下来该怎么办。

sentences.en: Ambivalence is an important signal that shows you that a rewarding and valuable relationship poses significant costs too, nudging you to ask whether to repair, recalibrate or step back.
sentences.cn: 矛盾心理是一个重要的信号：它告诉你，一段有回报、有价值的关系同时也意味着不小的代价，它推着你去追问——是修复，是重新调整，还是退后一步。

sentences.en: All this means that if you are now recognising for the first time that a significant relationship in your life is ambivalent for you, this awareness is already an important first step.
sentences.cn: 这一切意味着，如果你此刻第一次意识到：自己生命中某段重要的关系让你心怀矛盾，那么这份觉察本身已经是重要的第一步。

sentences.en: Becoming aware of your mixed feelings creates an opportunity to reflect on the relationship.
sentences.cn: 觉察到自己的复杂感受，为反思这段关系创造了机会。

sentences.en: This is a good moment to intervene and influence what happens next.
sentences.cn: 此时正是介入并影响后续走向的好时机。

sentences.en: After all, if you are having these mixed feelings, it means two helpful conditions are present:
sentences.cn: 毕竟，你之所以有这些复杂感受，说明两个有利条件已经具备：

sentences.en: There’s still some positivity to build on.
sentences.cn: 其一，还有一些积极面可供依托。

sentences.en: The relationship has rewards; the task is to reduce the negativity, not to build positivity from scratch; and
sentences.cn: 这段关系仍有回报；要做的功课是减少消极，而不是从零开始建立积极；并且

sentences.en: You are still engaged.
sentences.cn: 其二，你仍然是投入的。

sentences.en: You care, you’re motivated, and you’re open to making things better – whether through conversation, reflection, counselling or other forms of support (in other words, you are not in the indifferent quadrant of our framework, which would be worse news for the relationship!)
sentences.cn: 你在乎，你有动力，你也愿意把事情变好——无论是通过交谈、反思、心理咨询还是其他形式的支持（换句话说，你还不在我们框架里的冷漠象限——那对这段关系来说是更坏的消息！）

sentences.en: If negativity comes to overwhelm the positives – or if you find yourself starting to drift into indifference – then your window for change will have narrowed.
sentences.cn: 如果负面感受最终压过了正面感受——或者你发现自己开始滑向冷漠——那么你做出改变的窗口就会变窄。

sentences.en: Ambivalence, in contrast, sits in a workable in‑between zone, where effort still has room to make a difference.
sentences.cn: 相比之下，矛盾心理恰好坐落在一个仍可着力的中间地带，努力还有空间改变现状。

sentences.en: It can be a moment to approach the other person, communicate your needs, and see whether you can find ways together that allow the relationship to improve.
sentences.cn: 它可以成为一个契机：走近对方，说出你的需要，看看你们能否一起找到让关系变好的办法。

sentences.en: After all, ambivalence is the emotional equivalent of a blinking yellow light: not a stop, not a go, but an invitation to pay attention.
sentences.cn: 毕竟，矛盾心理在情绪上正是一盏闪烁的黄灯：不是停，不是行，而是一个提醒你留心的邀请。

sentences.en: And with the right attention, many relationships can still find their better path.
sentences.cn: 只要给以恰当的关注，许多关系依然能找到更好的那条路。
